react_result.final_narrative_text: The treatment group exhibits profound disruption of arachidonic acid–derived eicosanoid signaling. Cross-paradigm convergence on Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) — identified by RaMP multi-DB ORA (FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴) and independently by Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis (p = 0.0014) — is the dominant winner. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently retrieves the equivalent KEGG:hsa00590 pathway (4 shared hit compounds: arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE). Five of the eight input metabolites map to this pathway cluster, making arachidonic acid the hub driver. Its oxygenated products 5-HETE and 15-HETE, generated by 5-lipoxygenase (ALOX5) and 15-lipoxygenase (ALOX15) respectively, are the primary signal compounds. 15-Deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ2 provides a secondary prostaglandin-family hit consistent with the cyclopentenone PG branch. Methionine and cysteine metabolism is a second, smaller cross-paradigm signal (MetaboAnalystR p = 0.005, Mummichog p = 0.048) driven by L-cysteine and L-cystathionine, consistent with trans-sulfuration pathway perturbation. Mercaptopurine (purine-6-thiol) is flagged in RaMP's Selenium micronutrient network as a non-standard hit; its thio-moieties interact with selenoprotein synthesis pathways, suggesting an independent nucleotide/Purine metabolism effect distinct from the lipid axis.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on two distinct metabolic axes. RaMP multi-DB ORA retrieves Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top hit with FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴ and a fold enrichment of 1,429, driven by leukotriene A4, arachidonic acid, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently identifies Arachidonic acid metabolism (MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism) as the top pathway (p = 0.0017), with the same five input lipids as overlapping metabolites. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms Arachidonic acid metabolism (KEGG:hsa00590) with L-cysteine and L-cystathionine driving a secondary cysteine/methionine axis (hsa00670, p = 0.005; hsa00270, p = 0.008). The convergence across ORA and network-based methods on arachidonic acid as the primary hub, and on cysteine/methionine metabolism as a secondary signal, defines the biological phenotype. Mercaptopurine, resolved as a purine analog, independently flags purine nucleotide metabolism disruption consistent with its known pharmacology (PMID:40662363).

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on a dominant Eicosanoid synthesis signal. RaMP multi-database ORA retrieves Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked hit with FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴, driven by five input lipids: leukotriene A4, arachidonic acid, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. KEGG-specific PSEA via MetaboAnalystR independently recovers arachidonic acid metabolism (hsa00590) as its top hit (p = 2.49 × 10⁻⁶), covering the same four lipid input compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently identifies Eicosanoid synthesis as a top-2 hit (p = 0.00109), confirming the signal through mass-feature heuristics. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) anchors the enrichment as the canonical substrate of PTGS1 (COX-1) reaction R02377 in the eicosanoid cascade. Mercaptopurine is resolved as purine-6-thiol (CHEBI:2208) but is not a member of the eicosanoid pathway, placing it outside the primary signal. Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15) ranks second in RaMP ORA (FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴) and includes L-cysteine and L-cystathionine alongside the lipid drivers, consistent with selenol amino-acid biochemistry.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on a dominant Eicosanoid synthesis signal. RaMP multi-database ORA retrieves Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) as the top-ranked hit with FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴, driven by five input lipids: leukotriene A4, arachidonic acid, 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-prostaglandin J2, 5-HETE, and 15-HETE. KEGG-specific PSEA via MetaboAnalystR independently recovers arachidonic acid metabolism (hsa00590) as its top hit (p = 2.49 × 10⁻⁶), covering the same four lipid input compounds. Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis independently identifies Eicosanoid synthesis as a top-2 hit (p = 0.00109), confirming the signal through mass-feature heuristics. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) anchors the enrichment as the canonical substrate of PTGS1 (COX-1) reaction R02377 in the eicosanoid cascade. Mercaptopurine is resolved as purine-6-thiol (CHEBI:2208) but is not a member of the eicosanoid pathway, placing it outside the primary signal. Selenium micronutrient network (WP:WP15) ranks second in RaMP ORA (FDR = 6.18 × 10⁻¹⁴) and includes L-cysteine and L-cystathionine alongside the lipid drivers, consistent with selenol amino-acid biochemistry.
